scripts.radio:
Habari zenu na karibuni kwa Kenya on Record. Today, we bring you encouraging news on the public health front, but with a firm reminder that vigilance remains our best defense. Kenya has now marked eighteen consecutive days without a single new confirmed Ebola case. Even better, all six patients who were admitted to isolation facilities have made a full recovery and returned home to their families.

This outcome reflects the dedication of our frontline healthcare workers, community health promoters, and rapid response teams who acted swiftly to isolate and treat the infections. However, accountability requires that we do not drop our guard prematurely. Standard public health protocol requires forty-two consecutive days—two full incubation cycles—without a single new infection before an outbreak can be declared officially over. That means we are not yet halfway through the monitoring window.

County health departments must maintain active surveillance, especially at border entry points and transit hubs. Emergency allocations must continue supporting hospital preparedness rather than being redirected now that the immediate panic has subsided. As citizens, let us continue practicing proper hand hygiene and reporting any suspected symptoms to public health desks immediately.

Kwa ufupi: Kenya imerekodi siku kumi na nane bila kisa kipya cha Ebola, na wagonjwa wote sita wamepona kikamilifu na kuruhusiwa kwenda nyumbani. Hata hivyo, tuko bado kwenye kipindi cha uangalizi wa siku arobaini na mbili kabla ya kutangazwa tuko salama kabisa. Tuendelee kudumisha usafi na kutoa taarifa mapema.
scripts.voice_note: Habari zenu, this is Kenya on Record with your weekly update. Some good news on the public health front: Kenya has now gone eighteen straight days without recording any new Ebola case. Even better, all six patients who were in isolation have fully recovered and been discharged. This is solid proof that early detection and proper clinical care work. But we cannot afford to relax just yet. International health guidelines require forty-two consecutive days without a case before a country is officially declared Ebola-free. That means county surveillance teams must stay sharp, screening at borders must continue, and we must keep observing basic hygiene. If you or anyone you know experiences sudden high fever or unexplained bleeding, report it to the nearest public health facility immediately. Let’s see this process through to the end.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: All 6 Ebola patients recovered under proper hospital care. Beware of herbal cures or fake kits sold online. Report scams and symptoms via 719.
scripts.reels: Eighteen days. Zero new Ebola cases. And all six patients in Kenya have fully recovered and returned home. That is a massive win for our frontline healthcare workers and early response teams. But the job isn't finished. Protocol demands forty-two clear days before Kenya is declared officially free of the outbreak. Border screening and hospital readiness must hold firm until the finish line. No dropping the ball.
